frequency_question: How often does major, complex omnibus legislation complete the full legislative process from introduction to presidential signature within a 49-day (or similar short-turnaround) window?
membership_rule: Includes major energy, infrastructure, or budget reconciliation packages; excludes routine appropriations, continuing resolutions, and single-topic minor bills.

cases.name: American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009

provenance_note: 5 cases named, 15 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (3.0x)
coverage_note: 5 named major hits under tight timelines; estimated 15 total serious attempts meeting the constraint threshold over the 30-year period.
known_gaps: Exact tracking of failed or abandoned omnibus drafts that never reached a floor vote is incomplete.
skeleton: Major omnibus bills enacted in recent decades divided by total major attempts that faced severe time constraints (fewer than 60 days remaining in a session or Congress).
multiplier: 5 hits out of 15 attempts where timeline was severely constrained to under 60 days.
validity_reason: Procedural rules of Congress regarding cloture, committee markup, and floor scheduling remain stable across multiple decades.
